examples.explanation: The aldehyde is the principal function and the ketone is expressed by the oxo prefix.
The longest chain is selected as the principal chain, consistent with the cited acid seniority rules.
The hydroxy group is expressed as a prefix in the presence of the aldehyde group.
The aldehyde is named by the carbaldehyde construction and the hydroxy group is expressed as hydroxymethyl.
The phenoxy substituent is retained in the aldehyde name.
Fluoro and methyl substituents are expressed on the benzaldehyde parent.
The example gives the preferred substitutive name and the functional class name.
The ketal example contrasts the substitutive and functional class names.
The example applies the two naming methods to a compound with two ketal functions.
The example shows ordered O-substituent naming for a mixed diketal.
The cyclic acetal is named as a heterocyclic compound, with a functional class alternative.
The cyclic ketal is named as a spiro compound under Section P-24.
The example includes the corrected bracketed preferred name and the functional class name.
The hemiacetal is shown with its preferred substitutive and functional class names.
The ketone derivative is denoted by the class name hemiketal.
The sulfur analogue is named substitutively and by functional class nomenclature.
Capital italic S and O locants provide structural specificity in the functional class name.
The mixed O/S ketal is represented by the preferred substitutive and functional class names.
The cyclic sulfur analogue is named as a heterocyclic compound and by functional class nomenclature.
The mixed selenium and sulfur analogue follows the sulfur naming treatment with Se and S locants.
The selenium cyclic ketal demonstrates the same treatment extended to selenium.
The sulfur hemiacetal is named by the hydroxy-parent-derived substitutive method and by functional class nomenclature.
The O/S hemiacetal demonstrates the monothiohemiacetal class name.
The mixed selenium and sulfur hemiketal follows the sulfur analogue treatment.

value.source_text: In the presence of an aldehyde group, ketones, pseudoketones, heterones, hydroxy compounds, amines, and imines are expressed by prefixes.

value.rule: seniority for numbering polyfunctional aldehydes follows the seniority described for acids
value.source_text: Seniority for numbering polyfunctional aldehydes follows that described for acids.

value.ketal_subclass: neither R nor R' may be hydrogen

methods.construction: alkoxy, alkyloxy, aryloxy, etc. derivatives of an appropriate parent hydride or functional parent compound
cite the aldehyde or ketone, the O-substituents in alphanumerical order if required, and finally acetal or ketal

value.source_text: Acetals (ketals) are named in two ways; method (1), the substitutive method, leads to preferred IUPAC names.

cyclic_ketal.method: name as a spiro compound under Section P-24

general_nomenclature.allowed_method: functional class nomenclature using the appropriate divalent substituent groups

value.source_text: Cyclic acetals as the principal function are named as heterocyclic compounds; cyclic ketals are spiro compounds named in accordance with Section P-24; functional class nomenclature may be used in general nomenclature.

functional_class_method.hemiketal: use the class name hemiketal for ketone derivatives

value.preferred_method: substitutive alkoxy, alkyloxy, aryloxy, etc. derivative of an appropriate hydroxy parent compound such as an alcohol
value.source_text: These substitutive names are the preferred IUPAC names; other names use functional class nomenclature.

value.analogue_treatment: selenium, tellurium, and mixed chalcogen analogues are treated in the same way as sulfur analogues
value.preferred_method: substitutive alkylsulfanyl, arylsulfanyl, alkoxy, or aryloxy derivatives of a parent hydride
value.source_text: Substitutive names are preferred IUPAC names; other names can be generated by functional class nomenclature.

value.analogue_treatment: selenium, tellurium, and mixed analogues are treated in the same way as sulfur analogues
